newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: OECD chief says Slovak membership possible in '97.
newsitem.headline: OECD chief says Slovak membership possible in '97.

text.p: Slovakia may gain membership of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) by the end of this year, OECD General Secretary Donald Johnston said on Tuesday.

"I can't give a specific date, but I would think that it would be sometime in 1997, though I am not sure what stage the committee examinations are at," he told a news conference at a forum on European Banking in Prague.

Johnston recently said the examination process for Slovak membership to the Paris-based OECD was "quite far advanced", though some OECD officials said some outstanding issue, such as privatisation of the financial sector, remained to be addressed.

Slovakia has posted some of the strongest economic results of the nations to emerge from communist East Europe with 1996 GDP growth of 6.9 percent, and year-on-year inflation at a region-wide low of 6.0 percent.
But the country's image has suffered from Western rebukes that it is lagging behind in democratic reforms.
